DEC-003.title: Milestone v2.19 direction: verify + converge neural parallel-training surfaces (TensorParallelMatmul, SequenceParallel) onto the verified real-multi-GPU layer
DEC-003.rationale: v2.15-v2.18 converged and verified every high-level distributed op on the verified NCCL layer (distributed ops, distributed matmul, MeshBarrier) - RIL graph now has zero active tasks. The largest remaining never-run multi-GPU surface is the neural parallel-training layer: TensorParallelMatmul multi-GPU execution has no real multi-GPU test (tests/neural/tensor_parallel_test.cpp checks only buffer-size formulas and profiler math), and SequenceParallel tests pass comm=nullptr so they never drive a real NCCL collective. Static read of src/cuda/neural/tensor_parallel_matmul.cpp shows strong bug smells: ColumnParallel partitions B/C as contiguous slices (column-major semantics) while RowParallel slices A as contiguous rows (row-major), the SAME matrix order cannot satisfy both, recv_buffer is dead code, every rank redundantly computes ALL slices with the full B buffer, local_n = n/tp_degree drops remainders, and there is no divisibility guard. The R15-R18 pattern is that every never-run multi-GPU surface hides real bugs, so this path is expected RED. Plan: (P1) real thread-per-rank multi-GPU execution tests vs single-GPU reference (RED evidence); (P2) correct the partition/layout math on the verified NCCL layer and prove numerical equivalence; (P3) drive SequenceParallelAttention gather/scatter/all-reduce with a real NcclContext communicator, then optionally scale to 4/8 GPUs (host has 8x A100).
DEC-003.alternatives_rejected: MPI enablement is env-bound (no MPI headers on host); inference-layer multi-GPU (FlashAttention/PagedAttention) is a larger follow-up that depends on the sequence-parallel verification here; pure 8-GPU scale-up of already-green suites adds confidence but no new verified surface.

DEC-007.rationale: TASK-010 is the only active high-priority task: the v1.3 layer wrappers own no weights and forward() throws (DEC-006 fail-fast disposition). To close them we implement true weight-sharded layers: ColumnParallelLayer holds per-rank column shard [k x out/tp] (forward = local shard matmul -> sharded output, no comm); RowParallelLayer holds per-rank row shard [k/tp x n] (forward = local matmul on sharded input + block AllReduce -> replicated output); TensorParallelMLP = SiLU-gated FFN (gate/up ColumnParallel, down RowParallel). This is the only semantics that keeps the layer stack coherent (header docs match: col shards output, row consolidates to full width) and actually achieves weight sharding. Rank resolved via ctx.rank_of_device (v2.20 verified convention); per-instance stream-bound cuBLAS handle for thread-per-rank safety; shape rejection on non-divisible dims; single-GPU full-weight reference parity is the acceptance gate (v2.19/v2.20 pattern). API changes (explicit in_features/out_features instead of rigid 3*hidden_dim QKV) are safe: zero callers in the tree. Multi-commit diff exceeds the 300-line default because it replaces a stub surface + adds tests + a silu_and_mul kernel; exception documented per skill rule 8.

DEC-020.title: NSCK v3: record the writer's rank id (active_rank convention) so load rejects a same-topology file from another rank
DEC-020.rationale: TASK-063 is the silent-wrong-shard hazard: the NSCK v2 header stores the TP degree (mismatch rejected) but not the rank id, so a same-topology checkpoint written by another rank passes every size check and is restored silently. Fix: bump kVersion to 3 and add a u32 rank field after tp (both trainers). The rank is resolved at save/load via the v2.20 verified active_rank convention (cudaGetDevice -> ctx.rank_of_device) that the TP layers already use — this makes wrong-shard detection automatic, consistent with the library's rank model (raw device indices are wrong for non-default NcclContextConfig groups), and needs no caller discipline. tp<=1 -> rank 0 (single shard is shard 0; an uninitialized ctx cannot answer rank_of_device and must not throw). Load validates frank == shard_rank in the two-phase pre-apply header, so a cross-rank file throws with the trainer untouched. Trainers retain a non-owning NcclContext& ctx_ (matching the layer stack's ctx_ convention) to resolve the rank; the ctor signature is unchanged.
DEC-020.alternatives_rejected: explicit rank parameter on save_state/load_state (relies on caller discipline — the same weak per-rank-file-naming contract this task exists to remove; and a defaulted rank would let rank 1 silently accept rank 0's shard, recreating the bug); capturing the rank into the trainer at construction (adds a ctor-time resolve/throw path and changes behavior for every trainer even those that never checkpoint); deriving rank from the raw CUDA device index (wrong for non-default NCCL groups — the documented v2.20 pitfall)

DEC-021.title: TASK-065 v1 resolution: revert the library-level primary-context staleness machinery; keep the harmless cudaDeviceReset removals; the full-suite single-process NCCL run is not a supported configuration
DEC-021.rationale: Empirically, the v2.19 'context reset is undetectable' claim holds on this platform: (1) after cudaDeviceReset, cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain returns the SAME CUcontext pointer (driver reuses the freed chunk), so handle-identity comparison cannot detect the reset; (2) touching the stale handles (cudaStreamQuery / cudaStreamDestroy / ncclCommDestroy / ctx.destroy) crashes nondeterministically (core dump), so rebuild-via-destroy is unsafe; (3) a discard-and-leak rebuild would leak valid NCCL comms on the common no-reset path (device memory). A reliable automatic heal is therefore not achievable cheaply. Meanwhile the repo's supported verification already avoids the hazard: the full in-process baseline runs WITHOUT NCCL (multi-GPU suites self-skip -> 1482/0), and the multi-GPU suites are run separately with NCCL_TESTS_AVAILABLE=1. Within a supported multi-GPU-friendlies process (no single-GPU reset suites interleaved) all 45 multi-GPU tests pass, and after removing the 3 pointless cudaDeviceReset calls in CPU-only/single-GPU suites adjacent to multi-GPU boundaries the previously-hanging repro runs hang-free. Keep those removals; TASK-065 closes as hygiene + documented non-support of full-suite NCCL single-process runs.
DEC-021.alternatives_rejected: primary-context handle detection (pointer reused after reset — empirically refuted); rebuild-via-destroy (stale-handle destroy crashes nondeterministically); discard-bookkeeping-and-leak (leaks valid comms' device memory on the common path); removing ALL interleaved reset sites (~8 more suites, some load-bearing — whack-a-mole with destabilization risk and no supported-config benefit)

ISS-006.title: cuda::graph::pagerank() is directionally wrong and never converges
ISS-006.description: Two defects in src/cuda/graph/pagerank.cu: (1) pagerank_score_kernel gathers rank contributions from each vertex's OUT-neighbors (prev[columns[i]]/outdegree), but CSR rows hold out-neighbors, so it must gather from IN-neighbors to compute PR(v); the result never differentiates ranks correctly. (2) pagerank() computes delta = compute_pagerank_delta(result.ranks, result.ranks) comparing ranks to themselves, so it always exits after iteration 1 with final_delta 0 ('converged in 1 iterations'). Both confirmed by directed-path test (expected r0=0.05,r1=0.0925 but got uniform) and example output. pagerank_test.cpp had zero real graph invocations.
